evidence: Partial actual native and Terraform evidence. See the variant reports. A failed strict plan is not lifecycle success.
safety: Use an official Terraform release and the checked-in AWS 6.68.0 checksum lock with the prepared provider mirror. Do not downgrade the provider.
Install examples/requirements.txt in a caller-owned Python environment before execution.
All runs use examples/local.py local credentials, signed loopback clients and owned workspace/controller helpers. No native AWS mutation is required.
Controller account must match the explicit fixture account. The default is 738492615083. A caller-owned ASG runtime can use --account-id. Its endpoint remains running until its owner stops it.
Prepare actual images, Lambda static helpers, ECS systemd/cgroup-v2, QEMU/KVM firmware/guests, k3d and ALB relay before the applicable run. Runners never fabricate readiness or pull missing images.

Terraform creates owned IAM role/policy prerequisites with official service trust, reads them through data aws_iam_role, and destroys them after dependent compute resources. No seed database or cross-cohort role names are required.
Terraform state, token kubeconfigs and sensitive variables stay in private owned run subdirectories. Do not commit retained state or credentials. No ignore_changes masks unsupported settings.
Use a fixture-owned controller for Lambda/ECR, ECS and EKS. These fixtures stop and reopen the same controller database. Do not pass --endpoint to them.
Short-lived ECR credentials and EKS tokens use separate read-only Terraform state. Their timestamps must not change the infrastructure plan.

A failed no-change assertion remains a failure. The runner records it and continues the independent import, update, reopen and teardown stages. It raises all recorded failures before it can report lifecycle success.
ECS deployment reads use native task health and the retained rollout state. SQLite retains actual finish times and retired deployment history. A running but unhealthy task cannot produce SUCCESSFUL.
Cluster capacity updates admit only the configured FARGATE backend. SPOT and custom providers remain unsupported. A live provider-backed task or service prevents removal of its capacity association.
EKS admits the provider's disabled Auto Mode defaults. Enabled compute, load balancing and block storage remain unsupported.
ALB validates downstream HTTP header syntax after native classification, forwards actual request trailers, and half-closes a rejected client before a bounded drain. It has no classifier fallback.

ECS count updates reuse the admitted task roles. CreateService and explicit task-definition updates still check iam:PassRole. Application Auto Scaling does not need permission to pass an unchanged customer task role.

source_fixes: Persist actual ECS deployment finish times and retired history in migration 419. Register scoped deployment reads and real FARGATE capacity-provider admission.
Do not repeat iam:PassRole for an unchanged task definition during a count-only service update. Keep ordinary UpdateService authorization.
Accept only disabled EKS Auto Mode defaults. Empty log selection has no enabled streams.
Preserve EKS addon ModifiedAt during health observation. Actual operations still set the timestamp.
Import actual selected-platform image bytes directly into the ownership-verified Kubernetes worker. Official k3d import returned false success.
Select the Ready pod for the current revision before reading logs. A retiring pod is not the deployed revision.
Reject invalid downstream HTTP header names. Forward streamed trailers without copying the trailer map. Drain bounded rejected requests after write-half-close.
The ASG fixture consumes the SDK-decoded console text. It must not decode the same base64 data twice.
ASG accepts an explicit account and subnet. Shared fixture authentication checks that account.
ASG signed cleanup runs in finally, including failed native stages.
